source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Kidney dysfunction exclusively, with no infectious cause, which does not describe what an elevated lymphocyte count typically reflects","B":"Viral infections, since lymphocytes respond to viral pathogens, rather than the bacterial infection the colleague is currently assuming this pattern points toward","C":"Acute bacterial infection exclusively, with no other cause, similar to what the colleague is currently assuming this particular lab pattern indicates","D":"A normal finding with no clinical significance, contrary to what this significantly elevated lymphocyte percentage actually suggests"}}
source_row.rationale: Elevated lymphocyte percentage (lymphocytosis) is commonly associated with viral infections, since lymphocytes play a central role in the immune response against viral pathogens, though it can also occur with certain other conditions, distinct from neutrophilia, which is more classically associated with acute bacterial infection.
source_row.source_name: Clinical Laboratory Reference Standards — Lymphocyte Differential Interpretation
source_row.stem: A nurse reviews a client's WBC differential and notes a significantly elevated lymphocyte percentage, and a colleague assumes this pattern must point toward an acute bacterial infection needing antibiotics right away.
